event: On the ground at the launch wizard for VXE 758, the VXE SUAV GCS application appeared to close and reopen (screen flash) during mission sync and simulation; no flight impact.
component: VXE SUAV GCS application v6.4 window focus handling
failure_mode: During mission sync and simulation the GCS briefly hands window focus to another open application (Chrome) and back, seen as a flash; does not occur in 6.3.4 or with other apps minimized
contributing: Other applications (Chrome) open in the background on the GCS laptop

evidence.quote: It is quickly switching the active window to a chrome browser tab and back, similar to doing a quick Alt + Tab in windows.
It is only being experienced while other applications are open in the background.
I re-tested using 6.3.4 and did not experience the same issue.
I also was able to test this on two older GCS laptops we have lying around.

would_settle_it.what: Confirm the flash is a focus switch to the background Chrome window and not an application restart

would_settle_it.file: GCS 6.3.25 or other builds between 6.3.4 and 6.4.0
would_settle_it.what: Retest on intermediate GCS builds to find which change introduced the focus switching, as Ted requested

reasoning: The GCS does not actually close; the video shows it momentarily switching focus to a Chrome window. The behavior was reproduced on three laptops with GCS 6.4 only when another application was open, and did not occur after reverting to 6.3.4. That points to a regression in the 6.4 GCS window handling, but the specific code change was never identified.
notes: Severity 4 annoyance on the ground; ticket closed without a root cause or a test of intermediate GCS versions.

event: On the ground at HSV, the MagFit magnetometer calibration GUI on SGCS1 Kit 95 showed no data while VXE 758 was rotated through the six positions after the GCS 6.4 update.
component: MagFit application Windows Defender Firewall permission on GCS laptop
failure_mode: MagFit was not allowed through the Windows firewall (allowed app unchecked), so it received no data during mag cal
contributing: Firewall Allow Access prompt appears on first MagFit launch after the GCS 6.4 install and was not accepted
No guidance in the procedure on the firewall prompt (Service Bulletin was the corrective action)

evidence.quote: the MagFit GUI does not display any information while rotating the aircraft in any of the 6 listed positions
We just checked the GCS laptop and discovered that the MagFit app was deselected.
We allowed access and successfully completed a mag cal procedure with no issues.
if you go into the windows defender firewall → allowed apps the MagFit private needs to be checked

team_root_cause: MagFit was not allowed through firewall, suspected that operator did select allow during first Mag Cal after updating GCS to 6.4
reasoning: The MagFit GUI showed no data during calibration. Engineering suspected the firewall, the field team found the MagFit app unchecked in the Windows Defender Firewall allowed apps list, and after allowing it the mag cal completed normally. The fix test confirms the firewall block as the cause.
notes: The team Root Cause text says the operator 'did select allow', which reads as a typo for 'did not select allow' given the comments.

event: VXE 674 (fuel cell) at AEWE, Fort Benning, descended in VTOL onto a Primary LZ about 50 m from takeoff near trees, hit a tree branch after a late pause and wrong-direction nudges, and fell to the ground.
component: Primary LZ placement and landing pause/nudge commands
failure_mode: Primary LZ was set over or next to a treeline; operator paused late in the descent and the logged nudges were left and forward, toward the tree, instead of right
contributing: LZ may have been set with Use Vehicle Location while GPS was inaccurate (suggested, not confirmed)
Orbit change possibly not simulated and synced before RTB, so the vehicle flew the old mission
On-screen nudge buttons give much less authority than the joystick
Fuel cell kept running after impact and ignited pine needles

evidence.quote: Operator clicked nudge RIGHT a single time via the user interface.
Operator began pausing and logs indicated they nudged LEFT and FORWARD at this time.
The GCS does not change the LZ position unless the operator moved it manually.
When it finally did pause, it shifted a couple of feet to the left and collided with the branch of the tree.
I am not aware of any way the GCS will automatically move the LZ without operator interaction.

team_root_cause: System behaved as expected, operator error

would_settle_it.what: VTOL log ovrMode/ovrX/ovrY plot showing timing and direction of pause and nudges relative to the tree strike
GCS event log for the LZ edit, mission simulation and sync history before RTB
Mission file LZ coordinates compared with the intended safe landing spot

attachments_read: 29192_RMA Repair Quote for VXE-674 Warrranty EA Asset 250502-1 May 13, 2025.pdf.md
reasoning: VTOL logs show the vehicle did receive commands: one nudge right from the on-screen panel, then a pause with nudges left and forward just before it struck the branch, which matches the ground crew statement that it shifted left into the tree. Engineering states the GCS cannot move the LZ without operator action and a sync, so the LZ near the trees was an operator placement. The aircraft behaved as commanded; the crash came from LZ placement and late, wrong-direction nudging.
notes: Why the LZ ended up 50 m from takeoff (manual misplacement, Use Vehicle Location with poor GPS, or an unsynced mission edit) was never settled. RMA-682 repair quote lists both lift booms, left wing tip, air data pod, wing joiner and fuselage repair; an unrelated anti-spark NCR was raised during repair.

event: VXE 722 (PMA263 training) was sent to the LZ and began a VTOL descent from about 1,200 ft, became unresponsive to land immediately and pause, drifted about 800 m and crashed into trees.
component: VTOL AP landing state machine (dual land-immediately bug)
failure_mode: Land-immediately commands issued during the landing sequence left the VTOL controller in attitude control instead of position hold, so the vehicle drifted with the wind and ignored pause and nudge
contributing: Operator jumped to Primary LZ waypoint 4 and commanded VTOL from about 1,200 ft, beyond battery capacity
Vehicle battery below 15 percent before the landing
Repeated 'Climb abort, lift system fault' messages during descent
GCS 6.3.4 lacked the 6.4 interlock against VTOL at high altitude

evidence.quote: Time: 160:31.906  Change active waypoint: : Mission: Primary LZ  Waypoint: 4
Time: 155:59.531  Vehicle battery below 15 percent: 0.000000  0.000000
But with a cursory look I can confirm that multiple LI commands were issued, and the conditions to cause the state bug were there.
it does show VTOL going into Attitude mode while the FWAP is going into LI mode (states 400 to 500).
[10:50:20.594] VTOL MSG: Climb abort, lift system fault

team_root_cause:
Operator Error - Commanded Vehicle to VTOL at altitude.  v6.4 will have an interlock warning to help prevent this from occurring again. 
Bug- The unresponsive behavior came from the two land immediately commands during the landing sequence, leaving the VTOL controller in attitude control mode. This is a known issue.

would_settle_it.what: Synced VTOL/FWAP state overlay showing VTOL entering attitude mode during the land-immediately sequence
XCOMM event log sequence of LI request, LI abort and second LI request
FWAP and VTOL logs pulled after the crash, to confirm the attitude-mode state and lift system fault cause

attachments_read: 39019_S001369 ADS, Inc. - PMA-263 - VXE 722 Non-Warranty Replacement.pdf.md
39020_S001369 ADS, Inc. - PMA-263 - VXE 722 Non-Warranty Replacement (e4fa0c23-31fa-457a-a227-9a7b73df1b11).pdf.md
reasoning: The GCS event log shows a battery below 15 percent warning, then a jump to Primary LZ waypoint 4, which put the vehicle into VTOL at high altitude. The debug log shows land commands sent during the descent, and the engineer who synced the VTOL and FWAP logs found VTOL dropping into attitude mode while FWAP went to land-immediately, the known dual LI state bug. That bug explains the drift and the lack of response to pause; the operator action set it up.
notes: Debug log (about 500 KB) read by filtering out repeated landoverride, joystick and status lines and searching for VTOL messages, mode changes, LAND and PAUSE commands. Gain file (parameter dump) skimmed. Event log covers many earlier sessions; only the 04/12/25 session was read closely. The cause of the 'Climb abort, lift system fault' messages (likely low battery) was not investigated. RMA-672 photo PDFs have no text; aircraft was quoted for full replacement and returned unrepaired.

event: VXE 826 (Stalker Block 35X, non-released hardware and 6.4 firmware) lost GNSS in flight while approaching the PLZ, the VTOL landing drifted on dead-reckoned estimates, and the aircraft crashed on touchdown.
failure_mode: OEM7700 stopped sending heartbeats in flight (timeout, apparent reset) and did not re-initialize in the air; position estimates drifted
contributing: No in-air re-initialization of the GNSS receiver in this firmware
Possible power or Trellisware pylon interaction with the OEM7700 (under investigation, not confirmed)
Aircraft powered on for a long time on the ground before launch
Front cruise motor appeared to run with VTOL on during final

evidence.quote: based on the below first reported oem timeout the last heartbeat received before the timeout started was XComm CPU Time ~7,164.967.
then it pegged the velocity commands to try to get to the landing zone position
After plugging in the CW, the 7700 seems to finish initializing.
we don't have in-air re-init...
This incident was on non-released hardware and non-released software it should be part of the VXEP project.

would_settle_it.what: Hardware findings on OEM7700 power and why the receiver reset in flight
AAR and XCOMM logs around CPU time 7,165 s for 12 V rail and OEM serial traffic
Inspect avionics power feed to the OEM7700 and the receiver, and any NovAtel internal logs

reasoning: XCOMM logs show the OEM7700 heartbeat stopped at about 7,165 s, after which the vehicle flew on drifting estimates and pegged velocity commands toward the LZ. On the bench the receiver only finished initializing after a power cycle, and there is no in-air re-init. Why the receiver dropped (power, thermal, Trellisware interaction) was still under hardware investigation when the ticket was canceled.
notes: Ticket canceled as non-released hardware and software; comments are a pasted chat with repeated quotes. RMA-813 only says the aircraft needs motor replacement and was not repaired. The operator statement also describes odd transition behavior (turned right near IP5, VTOL and front motor on together) that was not analyzed.

event: On a VXE 401 (Vidar payload, Trillium gimbal) flight, after a mission sync the GCS lost contact with everything behind the aircraft Silvus radio; the aircraft flew its lost-link procedure and landed safely.
component: Aircraft internal Ethernet network between IPCOMM and XCOMM
failure_mode: Internal network path from the Silvus/IPCOMM side to XCOMM, VTOL and payloads dropped; repeatable on the ground only with two or more IP LWIR cameras and both lift booms connected, or after Aux payload power cycling
contributing: Third-party Vidar payload with multiple IP cameras
Skylink leaves unicast ports open to the SA camera, loading the link
Aux1/Aux2 payload power cycling
Possible ground loop (theory only)

evidence.quote: We still had good coms to the Silvus on the bird but could not ping the XCOM, VTOL, Gimbal, Payload, SA...
The Stalker did its lost coms procedures well and landed safely.
4/28-210pm: customer states, can access ipcomm via silvus RF, but unable to get to xcomm. (seems more like xcomm ethernet chip issue then)
We tried replicating it three times afterwards and didn't get the issue to show up.
Lost comms occurs at the drop off.

team_view_in_comments: seems more like xcomm ethernet chip issue then

would_settle_it.what: XCOMM network traffic per port at the moment of the drop to see which switch port lost link
XCOMM switch port status and event log during the 5/20 preflight recurrence

would_settle_it.file: XCOMM and IPCOMM switch hardware with Vidar payload
would_settle_it.what: Bench test with the payload configuration to isolate whether the XCOMM Ethernet switch, IPCOMM or payload loading drops the link

reasoning: With the fault present, the Silvus was reachable over RF but nothing behind it, and a hardline connection reached XCOMM and VTOL but not the Silvus, so the break is inside the aircraft network between the radio side and XCOMM. The customer later reached IPCOMM over RF but not XCOMM, which points toward XCOMM side Ethernet, but this was never confirmed and the issue could not be reproduced. The lost-link landing worked as designed.
notes: Resolution Cannot Reproduce; added to a 'Bermuda Triangle' list. Ticket also notes separate bus/vaux faults during VTOL landing, thought to be a gimbal stuck in retract, probably unrelated. Linked VXEP-1307/XKIT-4730 (VXE 376, fuel cell grounding suspected) and VXEP-1310 (VXE 689, dead Silvus radio) are similar symptoms on other aircraft, not this one.

event: Flying VXE 336 over the ocean from an island, when terrain data changed from 0 to no DTED the waypoint altitudes mixed MSL and AGL references, causing unwanted climbs and descents until the operator switched to U-Drive.
component: GCS waypoint altitude MSL/AGL conversion when DTED is unavailable
failure_mode: With no DTED, AGL altitudes were computed using GCS field elevation instead of sea level, so 1400 ft AGL became about 2200 ft MSL and editing one field corrupted the other
contributing: Flying from an island with an 800 ft drop-off over water with no terrain data

evidence.quote: the way points seem to get messed up between MSL and AGL being the same.
I was able to stop the unwanted climbs or descents by switching to udrive.
I also disabled auto AGL and auto LOS to see if that made a difference.

would_settle_it.what: Mission and log data showing commanded MSL and AGL altitudes and terrain elevation source when DTED changed to none

reasoning: The operator describes waypoint MSL and AGL values diverging only after the DTED readout changed from 0 to none, with AGL apparently referenced to the GCS field elevation. That narrows it to altitude reference handling with missing terrain data, most likely in the GCS where the waypoint fields are edited. No log analysis was done and engineering said it would need more investigation, so the module is not confirmed.
notes: Closed as Not Verifiable; only the operator statement and an unconverted zip are available. Whether the conversion happens in the GCS or the autopilot is not stated.

event: On 6 Dec 2024 at Fort Carson, VXE 541 failed to transition to VTOL lift on landing, kept slowing in fixed-wing flight and glided into the ground.
component: AS150 power contact, center wing to HLB connector
failure_mode: HLB connector not fully seated: marginal contact (about 5.7 ohm) limited lift current to about 5 A versus about 180 A needed, so lift motors could not start and the landing aborted into a lift system fault
contributing: Known dimensional tolerance mismatch between center wing male pins and HLB female sockets (assembly predates dimensional sorting)
Possibly not enough force applied by the operator when seating the HLB
Solder flow found in the center wing HLB connector
Landing state machine in LAND_WAITTRANS could not abort safely

evidence.quote: The HLB battery connection was not fully connected due to a previously identified dimensional tolerance issue or not enough force was applied when seating the connector by the operator.
Contact resistance measured 5.7 ohms approximately
Note: Low Current levels ~5 Amps vs typical ~180 Amps
Lift system did not pull expected power during landing. Current levels remain under 5 amps until the end.
he found solder flow in the Hybrid Lift Battery connector on the center wing.

team_root_cause: Connector was loosely mated to the HLB from the CW.

would_settle_it.what: Measure the HLB female socket diameters and contact force to confirm whether the part or the seating was at fault

attachments_read: 29105_F-855-002 Rev B - Edge Autonomy Return Authorization (RMA) Customer Form (VXE541).pdf.md
reasoning: XCOMM logs show repeated low-power and power-difference lift faults during the landing, and VTOL and XCOMM data both show lift current under about 5 A against about 180 A expected, with HLB voltage dips to near zero. The investigation measured about 5.7 ohm through the connector and found the center wing pins undersize relative to the HLB sockets, and the FSR found solder flow in the center wing HLB connector. Bench tests found XCOMM and VTOL working, so the marginal HLB connection is the cause.
notes: Whether the initiator was the known pin/socket tolerance issue or operator seating force is left open by the report; I chose manufacturing_quality since the assembly predates dimensional sorting. A hardware engineer comment in FS2-3321 suggested a lift ESC problem, but later data and testing pointed to the connector. Material disposition calls for replacing the dual current sense board, noting its connector was suspected as the initial failure. Purchase order and quote attachments are commercial only.

event: Internal B30 asset VXE 689 came back from Huntsville with a non-working MCM (mission computer); the nose fuse was found blown, so the MCM had no power.
failure_mode: Nose fuse blown, removing power to the MCM; cause of the overcurrent not found
contributing: MCM was on a non-flight-critical power bus (corrective action moves it to the flight critical bus)
Aircraft used for display at a demo with no usage or configuration records

evidence.quote: 689 came back from Huntsville with a blown Nose Fuse, so no power was getting to the MCM.
The data logs will definitely tell you when the fuse was blown
Internal asset with no records of usage or config. Closing Issue.

team_view_in_comments: 689 came back from Huntsville with a blown Nose Fuse, so no power was getting to the MCM.

would_settle_it.what: Power data around the time the nose fuse opened to identify the overcurrent source
Check the fused circuit and MCM for a short

reasoning: The Issue Status states the nose fuse was blown and no power reached the MCM, and replacing it fixed the symptom. What blew the fuse was never investigated because the internal asset had no usage records and the ticket was canceled. So the failure is narrowed to the fused MCM power feed, not to the part that drew the overcurrent.
notes: Canceled as an internal, non-released system. Cloned into VXEP-1283 (VXE 300) and VXEP-1284 (VXE 757), which are separate events. Linked XKIT power budget tickets not read (design follow-up, not cause).

event: On 14 May 2025 the MCM on internal B30 asset VXE 300 dropped off the 10. aircraft network.
failure_mode: DHCP connection profile had a blank device field, so it could be applied to any adapter and the aircraft Ethernet randomly took a dynamic address instead of its static 10. address
contributing: MCM had been reflashed to Jetpack and modified with third-party (OKSI) scripts, not in production configuration

evidence.quote: Issue was that the device field on the DHCP connection profile was blank.
it was luck of the draw whether the aircraft Ethernet connection would get a static IP address or a dynamic one.
if 300 was configured like a production vehicle, it would not have had that issue
My suspicion is that one of them reset the ethernet interface settings.

team_root_cause:
had been set to be able to auto DHCP which let it randomly drop the 10. network, explanation from Jo B.:
"Issue was that the device field on the DHCP connection profile was blank. This means the DHCP connection profile could be (and was) applied to all network adapters.
To oversimplify a bit, it was luck of the draw whether the aircraft Ethernet connection would get a static IP address or a dynamic one."
300 has been played around with a bunch, reflashed to Jetpack
if 300 was configured like a production vehicle, it would not have had that issue
reasoning: The network engineer found the DHCP connection profile on the MCM had no device assigned, so it could be applied to the aircraft Ethernet adapter and replace the static 10. address. The MCM had been reflashed and altered with outside scripts and was not in production configuration. Fixing the profile resolved the issue.
notes: Canceled as an integration issue on non-released components. Cloned from VXEP-1282 (VXE 689 blown nose fuse, a different cause).
